analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, in the Runtime constants table (head lines ~2009-2012). It splits the coordinator reconnect backoff constants into a new CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift source, adds a 60s stable-session reset counted from the register frame, and adds a 0-1s randomized reconnect wait after close code 1012. The ping/pong row now cites CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift. I examined the supplied base text (lines 397-1270) and the patch. The base text is unchanged context, and I found no new security-relevant content in it. This is documentation only, with no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling changes in the supplied evidence. Relevant boundary: TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket), with availability considerations. The backoff reset after 60s stable and the short jitter on 1012 are reconnect-availability behavior documented here. They do not weaken the T-053 binding or revocation boundaries, because reconnect still requires fresh registration and authorization. Unverified contract: the actual CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift implementation is not supplied. Whether it matches these documented values, and whether the 1012 fast reconnect could cause thundering-herd load on the coordinator, cannot be confirmed from this evidence. The tight 0-1s range with no growth is a minor availability design point rather than a demonstrated vulnerability. Wider reconnect behavior is outside this review. No findings.
